account:
Today has been mostly quiet, but there has been repeated, unusually vague talk of a bridge or port change. I heard several townsfolk repeat it, sometimes naming the bakery or inn; one report placed the baker, freight and neighbour at the bakery. None of those reports explained what was changing or supplied firsthand evidence. At tea, my neighbour said the baker knew of no confirmed changes and that the neighbour had personally seen nothing unusual along the docks. I cannot tell whether this is a real proposal or simply circulating gossip, and I have no evidence of its purpose or of anyone deliberately organizing it.

My scheduled grain inspection at the mill could not be completed because I could not find the miller. The secretary also visited this afternoon to request another time and found nobody there. That leaves the inspection outstanding; absence alone does not establish anything suspicious. I have asked for a new appointment confirmed by the miller and for the inspection to remain marked incomplete.

No council letters, other correspondence, or urgent matters have reached the secretary today. The secretary reports the appointment book remains secure. The neighbour reported that the baker had stocked his stall and said there was plenty of bread; I have no firsthand evidence today of a shortage. I kept lunch, the council correspondence appointment, tea with the neighbour, and my afternoon return to the office. I am now at town hall with the secretary, who is to remain available for correspondence until I leave for home at seven.
